basis: Inherited dystonia; dysphonia, dysarthria and torticollis reflect neurologic motor dysfunction.
Macular coloboma and brachydactyly define the syndrome; absent or dysplastic nails occur in 30-79%. Renal agenesis occurs in only 5-29%.
Tumour originates in the pineal gland, an endocrine gland within the brain.
Benign female reproductive tract epithelial-stromal tumour, typically ovarian; reproductive organs have no axis.
Severe neurodevelopmental dysfunction and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome; optic atrophy affects 2/6 and strabismus 5/6.
Inherited immune dysregulation with cytopenias; inflammatory liver injury commonly exceeds 50% and CNS involvement ~30-50% in familial HLH; RHOG-specific frequencies uncertain.
Muscular dystrophy directly damages skeletal muscle; no evidence supplied for common additional organ damage.
Cardiac, ocular and radial malformations define the syndrome; anal atresia or displacement occurs in 30-79%. Ear/hearing abnormalities also reach 30-79% but exceed the cap.
Inherited corneal dystrophy affecting corneal epithelium and stroma.
Inflammation of the deep cornea; the umbrella does not establish an infectious or autoimmune cause.
Marrow failure is central to the ACD short-telomere spectrum; pulmonary fibrosis and mucocutaneous disease vary across presentations, without established ≥30% frequencies here.
Fibromuscular dysplasia directly affects extremity arterial walls; it is not an inflammatory vasculitis or skeletal muscle disease.
Deprivation amblyopia is a developmental loss of visual function; no separate neurologic disease is established.
